evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Fields and intent are explicit; no vague terms that allow materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Clear actionable artifact (URL) and purpose; no ambiguous terminology.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specifies input mechanism and intent precisely; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope and intent are clear (items in this session); wording is understandable without multiple material interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Action and outcome are explicit and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear user action and purpose; duplicated wording is stylistic, not semantic ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Clear intent (editing an item) and purpose; no vague terms.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Action and effect are explicit; no ambiguous terminology.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately ... even though not all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is explicitly defined (show immediately even if some haven't estimated), so not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Uses a standard term ('average') with an unambiguous mathematical meaning in most contexts; acceptable at story level.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Condition and expected behavior are specific and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Purpose is clear; 'agreed-upon' is standard collaborative concept and not materially ambiguous in this context.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Scope ('earlier in the session') and action are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Intent and artifact (spreadsheet) are clear; format details can be specified in acceptance criteria without this story being semantically ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Action and source are explicit; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Behavior and intent are clear; 'previous games' is unambiguous in context.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates
evaluations.rationale: Desired artifact (transcript) and contents are explicit; not vague.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: File format and artifact are explicit; not open to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Format and intent are explicit; any CSV specifics belong in acceptance criteria.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Effect of action (no longer stored) is explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation fields are explicitly listed; no vague language.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Authentication method is specified; any small ambiguity between 'account name' vs email is not materially different for this story-level requirement.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: High-level story acceptable; though fields to change are unspecified, this is typical and not inherently multi-interpretative at the story level.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Intent and effect are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Requirement is specific about timezone behavior and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Mechanism and channel are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies two concrete card sets and their intent; small use of 'etc.' doesn't produce materially different interpretations of the two sequences.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators ... large but not immense teams
evaluations.rationale: Phrase 'large but not immense teams' is subjective and could be interpreted differently; the qualifier is ambiguous and adds no precise requirement beyond 'up to 15'.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining mechanism and input are explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Clear intent and behavior; not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope ('this session') and artifact are clear; no materially different readings.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Behavior and purpose are explicit and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Condition and expected behavior are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Clear rule for when estimate changes are allowed; not open to multiple material interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Intent is understandable (prior estimates for the same story); possible edge cases (scope of 'prior') can be addressed in acceptance criteria but wording is not materially ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Scope ('current round') and visibility are explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and visibility are explicit; not subject to multiple material interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Trigger and behavior are explicitly stated; unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Action and scope ('prior rounds') are clear; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Behavior is precise (same order across draws) and not open to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Condition for change is explicit; not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Though 'small' is subjective, this is a minor UI sizing detail and not likely to cause materially different requirement interpretations at story level.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Does not specify which standards/versions or conformance level; that omission can lead to materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Intent is clear (provide definitions); 'commonly used terms' is natural for this type of story and not likely to cause materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'as fast as possible' is vague and can be interpreted in many ways (which queries, performance targets), leading to materially different technical work.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specific browser versions are listed; while 'function correctly' could be scoped later, the platforms are explicit so the story is not semantically ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Phrase 'where possible' is vague and leaves room for differing interpretations of required versus optional accessibility behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: The term 'quickly' is vague without performance targets and could be implemented in materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Requirement is clear and specific (support Unicode); not ambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: 'Sensible' and 'predictable' are subjective terms that can be interpreted differently by stakeholders, risking materially different URL designs.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Word 'nice' is subjective (look, content, information); without definition it allows different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: 'Non-identifiable' is ambiguous (anonymization vs pseudonymization, re-identification risk) and can lead to materially different data-handling requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Term 'some metrics' is vague and does not specify which metrics or scope, allowing materially different interpretations of what to implement.
